newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks rise on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: China stocks rise on technical rebound.

text.p: China's stock markets continued a technical rebound to end higher on Tuesday, but investors remained cautious following last week's government efforts to cool trading, brokers said.

Shanghai's B share index rose 3.332 points or 3.92 percent to 88.291 points on volume of 15.245 million shares worth $11.209 million, while Shenzhen's B index rose 2.53 points or 1.52 percent to 169.39 points on turnover of HK$87.3 million.

Brokers said Shanghai B shares rose on speculative buying as domestic institutions that suffered losses last week pushed up stocks in firms that have a heavy weighting in the index, triggering follow-up buying from retail investors.
"Some domestic institutions do not want to let the market fall because they hold large positions and need follow-up buying to create an opportunity for liquidation," one broker said.
"But market sentiment is still cautious amid talk of possible further crackdown measures from Beijing before too long," he said.
Shanghai Posts & Telecommunications Equipment was the star on speculative buying, surging $0.048 or 9.95 percent to $0.530 on volume of 175,500 shares.

Shenzhen's B index ended up after U.S. President Bill Clinton said he planned to renew China's most favoured nation (MFN) trade status, but profit-taking and fears of fresh government moves to cool the markets trimmed early gains, brokers said.
"The B index rallied in the morning on the MFN announcement, but some of the effect wore off in the afternoon," a trader at J&A Securities said.
Shanghai's A share index rose on institutional buying in blue chips, but trading remained cautious amid market uncertainties, brokers said.
The A index rose 37.746 points or 2.68 percent to 1,444.218 points on volume of 497.0 million shares worth 7.2 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index jumped 179.531 points or 4.58 percent to 4,101.820 points.

Shenzhen A shares gained 14.40 points or 3.05 percent to 486.83 on turnover of 9.4 billion yuan after Shenzhen Development Bank Co hit its 10 percent limit-up at 40.67 yuan despite Monday's announcement of the bank's probe into its own stock trading irregularities.
"Unless all market rumours, including government suspension of major brokerages trading for their own accounts, are confirmed, the indices will not fall in the short term," said a broker.
"But after last week's lesson, institutions might reduce their momentum to push the markets higher on fears of triggering an official crackdown," he said.
